thread.title: Facebook is in bear-market territory as Apple flirts with a correction, and they are far from alone

author: morningstar.com
title: Facebook is in bear-market territory as Apple flirts with a correction, and they are far from alone
text:
By Wallace Witkowski, MarketWatch
About 65% of tech sector in correction territory, while about 1 in 5 tech companies are experiencing a bear market
After the worst quarter for stocks in more than two years and another decline at the beginning of a new quarter Monday, nearly a fifth of the S&P 500's tech sector closed in bear territory, led by Facebook Inc.'s decline of more than 20%.
About 65% of the sector is in correction territory, with big names like Apple Inc. (AAPL) , Intel Corp. (INTC) and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) flirting with correction levels. Earlier Monday, shares of Apple and Intel were more than 10% off their recent highs, but both closed the session at about 9% off those highs. Some big tech companies, like Google parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) (GOOGL), are already in a correction and are approaching bear levels.
Read more about bear markets and corrections (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/was-that-a-stock-market-crash-do-the-math-and-check-the-yield-curve-2018-02-06)
A bear market is defined as 20% or more off the stock's 52-week high, while a correction is 10% or more off the 52-week high. Tech stocks have an increasingly large effect on stock indexes because of their weighting: The sector accounts for $6.473 trillion, or about 28%, of the S&P 500's $23.438 trillion in market cap spread across 11 sectors, according to FactSet data.
On Monday, 13 out of the 69 tech stocks on the S&P 500 index finished 20% or more off their 52-week high, or at bear levels.

Out of those 13 stocks, the hardest hit subsector is chips, with Broadcom, Qualcomm, Micron, AMD and Qorvo all in bear territory. The PHLX Semiconductor Index is 12.8% off its 52-week high set in mid-March, compared with the S&P 500's decline of 10.1% from its 52-week high, which was set in late January. Over the past 12 months, the SOX index is up 26%, compared with the 9.3% gain on the S&P 500.
Large-cap tech companies -- those worth $100 billon or more -- that are already in correction territory include Alphabet, with shares more than 15% off their 52-week high; along with Cisco Systems Inc. (CSCO) , 11.2% off; International Business Machines Corp. (IBM) , off 14.9%; Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) , off 13.1%; and Oracle Corp. (ORCL) , off 15.8%.
Shares of Microsoft and Adobe Systems Inc. (ADBE) are flirting with entering correction territory, with both stocks more than 8% off their 52-week highs.
